subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these goal records.

judge.implied_focus: The nature and quality of each improvement goal -- characterizing what each goal aims to improve, how, at what scale, and how well-specified/measurable its target is.

per_column.name: improvement_domain
per_column.rationale: Captures the substantive area a goal targets (satisfaction, revenue, cost), a core facet of characterizing the goal.

per_column.name: primary_action_lever
per_column.rationale: Identifies the mechanism/means used to pursue the goal, a coherent 'how' facet.

per_column.name: target_metric_type
per_column.rationale: Classifies how the target is expressed, directly relevant to goal measurability.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Adds a temporal facet to goal characterization, useful for prioritization.

per_column.name: improvement_magnitude_band
per_column.rationale: Bands the ambition/size of the target, a meaningful facet of what's worth attention.

per_column.name: scope_of_change
per_column.rationale: Captures organizational reach, a coherent facet of goal significance.

per_column.name: has_baseline_value
per_column.rationale: Flags whether a goal is grounded/measurable -- a quality/rigor facet, highly actionable.

per_column.name: metric_category_alignment
per_column.rationale: Flags internal consistency between metric and category, a data-quality/attention facet.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively converge on one coherent, data-inferable focus: characterizing improvement goals along interpretable facets (what/how/scope/time/magnitude) plus quality/rigor flags (baseline presence, metric-category alignment). This is not a scattered grab-bag nor a mechanical set (no token counts or bare sentiment); each column extracts a semantically distinct, goal-relevant attribute. The structure is well-differentiated at a useful granularity, mixing categorical facets with quality flags that directly answer 'what's worth attention' (e.g., unbaselined or misaligned goals warrant scrutiny). Minor deductions: the focus is inferred/implicit rather than explicitly proposed, and a couple of facets (time_horizon, magnitude) partly re-encode existing date/target columns, slightly overlapping the original schema. Overall a strong, actionable realization of focus inference.
